challenges.title: AI vs ML Quick Check
challenges.description: Which statement correctly distinguishes AI and ML?

choices.text: AI is the broader field; ML is a subset focused on learning from data
ML is broader than AI and contains AI as a subset
AI and ML are unrelated fields
AI only works with robots, while ML only works with text

challenges.hint: Think about parent field vs subset.

solution.code: AI is the broader field; ML is a subset focused on learning from data

steps.title: Correct Solution
steps.explanation: The correct answer is: AI is the broader field; ML is a subset focused on learning from data.

steps.title: Why
steps.explanation: AI is the umbrella discipline that includes multiple approaches, and machine learning is one of those approaches.
steps.code: AI is the broader field; ML is a subset focused on learning from data

steps.title: Curiosity
steps.explanation: In everyday conversations, "AI" often refers to generative systems, but the field also includes planning, search, and robotics.

challenges.title: Structured or Unstructured?
challenges.description: A table with fixed columns for age, salary, and city is an example of:

choices.text: Structured data
Unstructured data
Streaming-only data
Synthetic data only

challenges.hint: Rows/columns with consistent schema indicate structure.

solution.code: Structured data

steps.title: Correct Solution
steps.explanation: The correct answer is: Structured data.

steps.title: Why
steps.explanation: Tabular records with fixed columns follow a predefined schema, which is the definition of structured data.
steps.code: Structured data

steps.title: Curiosity
steps.explanation: Most production ML systems combine structured tables with unstructured signals like text or images.

challenges.title: Feature or Label?
challenges.description: In a spam classifier, the email text is the input and spam/not-spam is the output. What is the output called?

choices.text: Label
Feature
Model
Dataset

challenges.hint: Features are inputs; labels are targets.

solution.code: Label

steps.title: Correct Solution
steps.explanation: The correct answer is: Label.

steps.title: Why
steps.explanation: The output the model must predict is the target variable, which in supervised learning is called the label.
steps.code: Label

steps.title: Curiosity
steps.explanation: A strong feature-label definition early in a project prevents many downstream data and evaluation mistakes.

challenges.title: Learning Type Match
challenges.description: Clustering customer records without known target values is:

choices.text: Reinforcement learning
Unsupervised learning
Transfer learning
Supervised learning

challenges.hint: No labels usually means unsupervised learning.

solution.code: Unsupervised learning

steps.title: Correct Solution
steps.explanation: The correct answer is: Unsupervised learning.

steps.title: Why
steps.explanation: Unsupervised learning works without target labels and focuses on finding patterns or groups in the data.
steps.code: Unsupervised learning

steps.title: Curiosity
steps.explanation: Many modern workflows combine supervised and unsupervised steps, such as pretraining then fine-tuning.

challenges.title: Classification or Regression
challenges.description: Predicting a house price in dollars is typically a:

choices.text: Clustering task
Regression task
Classification task
Dimensionality reduction task

challenges.hint: Numeric continuous target implies regression.

solution.code: Regression task

steps.title: Correct Solution
steps.explanation: The correct answer is: Regression task.

steps.title: Why
steps.explanation: When the target is a numeric value on a continuous scale, the problem type is regression.
steps.code: Regression task

steps.title: Curiosity
steps.explanation: Some business problems can be framed both ways, depending on whether you need exact values or categories.

challenges.title: Data quality: Concept check
challenges.description: Which description best captures Data quality?

choices.text: Data quality guarantees correct predictions whenever it is present.
Data quality removes the need for representative validation data.
Data quality is primarily a reporting label with no effect on an ML workflow.
Data quality is fitness of data for its intended use across accuracy, completeness, consistency, timeliness, and representativeness.

challenges.hint: Focus on the role, evidence, and boundary of Data quality; reject absolute claims that bypass validation.

solution.code: Data quality is fitness of data for its intended use across accuracy, completeness, consistency, timeliness, and representativeness.

steps.title: Decision: Data quality is fitness of data for its intended use across accuracy, completeness, consistency, timeliness, and representativeness.
steps.explanation: The best answer is “Data quality is fitness of data for its intended use across accuracy, completeness, consistency, timeliness, and representativeness.”

steps.title: Why this fits Data quality
steps.explanation: Data quality is fitness of data for its intended use across accuracy, completeness, consistency, timeliness, and representativeness. In practice, it is used to validate inputs before training and monitor them after deployment.

steps.title: Why the alternatives fail
steps.explanation: Option 1 is not acceptable because it either overclaims what Data quality can establish or bypasses evidence needed for the decision. Option 2 is not acceptable because it either overclaims what Data quality can establish or bypasses evidence needed for the decision. Option 3 is not acceptable because it either overclaims what Data quality can establish or bypasses evidence needed for the decision.

steps.title: How to apply the idea
steps.explanation: A strong workflow would define acceptance checks tied to the model and business risk. Evidence should include schema checks, missing-value rates, range checks, duplicate rates, and sampled record review.

steps.title: What to remember under exam pressure
steps.explanation: Remember the boundary: high-quality data cannot remove irreducible uncertainty or guarantee generalization Example: rejecting impossible ages and investigating a spike in missing income values.

choices.text: Metrics is primarily a reporting label with no effect on an ML workflow.
Metrics is quantitative summaries chosen to reflect model behavior and decision goals.
Metrics guarantees correct predictions whenever it is present.
Metrics removes the need for representative validation data.

challenges.hint: Focus on the role, evidence, and boundary of Metrics; reject absolute claims that bypass validation.

solution.code: Metrics is quantitative summaries chosen to reflect model behavior and decision goals.

steps.title: Decision: Metrics is quantitative summaries chosen to reflect model behavior and decision goals.
steps.explanation: The best answer is “Metrics is quantitative summaries chosen to reflect model behavior and decision goals.”

steps.title: Why this fits Metrics
steps.explanation: Metrics is quantitative summaries chosen to reflect model behavior and decision goals. In practice, it is used to compare systems using measures aligned with error consequences.

steps.title: Why the alternatives fail
steps.explanation: Option 1 is not acceptable because it either overclaims what Metrics can establish or bypasses evidence needed for the decision. Option 2 is not acceptable because it either overclaims what Metrics can establish or bypasses evidence needed for the decision. Option 3 is not acceptable because it either overclaims what Metrics can establish or bypasses evidence needed for the decision.

steps.title: How to apply the idea
steps.explanation: A strong workflow would define the decision and error costs before selecting metrics. Evidence should include multiple complementary metrics, baselines, uncertainty, slice analysis, and threshold context.

steps.title: What to remember under exam pressure
steps.explanation: Remember the boundary: no single metric captures every operational or fairness concern Example: using recall and review volume for a screening workflow rather than accuracy alone.

steps.title: Why this fits Precision
steps.explanation: Precision is the fraction of predicted positives that are truly positive. In practice, it is used to measure how trustworthy positive alerts are.

steps.title: Why the alternatives fail
steps.explanation: Option 1 is not acceptable because it either overclaims what Precision can establish or bypasses evidence needed for the decision. Option 2 is not acceptable because it either overclaims what Precision can establish or bypasses evidence needed for the decision.
